lessons.title: Do a capacity estimate before drawing boxes
lessons.detail: Both design rounds lost points on numbers: no traffic or storage estimate, then no basis for the design choices.
lessons.practice: For every design question, write 3 numbers first: requests/sec, data size per year, read/write ratio.

lessons.title: Ask clarifying questions before designing
lessons.detail: Jumped straight into components in the first design round.
lessons.practice: Spend the first 5 minutes on scope: users, scale, must-have features.

lessons.title: State time and space complexity before coding
lessons.practice: Say 'This is O(n log n) time, O(n) space' right after describing the approach.

lessons.title: Keep two questions ready for each interviewer
lessons.detail: Had no questions at the end of round 1. It can read as low interest.
lessons.practice: Ask about their team's work: 'What is the hardest problem your team solved this year?'

interviews.summary: Passed the coding round. Lost the system-design round: jumped into components before asking about scale.

rounds.name: Round 1 — Coding

questions.my_answer: Sort by start, merge in one pass.
questions.better_answer: Same — and state O(n log n) time, O(n) space before coding.

questions.q: Find the k most frequent words
questions.better_answer: Min-heap of size k: O(n log k). Mention the tie-break rule.

went_well: Talked through the approach before coding
went_wrong: Did not state complexity until asked

rounds.name: Round 2 — System design

questions.my_answer: Drew services and a DB right away.
questions.better_answer: First ask: reads/sec, writes/sec, URL lifetime, custom aliases. Then estimate storage, then design. Key choice: base62 ID from a counter vs a hash.

went_wrong: Ran out of time for the deep dive

interviews.summary: Two rounds done. Coding went well. Design round was better than last time but still short on numbers.

rounds.name: Round 1 — Coding

questions.my_answer: HashMap + doubly linked list, O(1) get/put.
questions.better_answer: Same. Also mention LinkedHashMap with accessOrder=true as the quick Java version.

went_well: Clean code, tested edge cases aloud

rounds.name: Round 2 — System design

questions.my_answer: Idempotency key table with a unique constraint.
questions.better_answer: Key + request hash stored with status (in-progress / done) and the saved response; return the saved response on retry; TTL for cleanup; reject a reused key with a different body.

questions.q: How many requests per second can one Postgres node take?
questions.better_answer: Give a range with reasons: a few thousand simple writes/sec on one node; reads scale with replicas and cache. Say the assumption out loud.

went_well: Asked clarifying questions first this time
